bullets: Three Ghosts: Past, Present, Yet to Come: the novella’s structure is built on time.
All the visits happen in **one night**; Scrooge marvels that ‘The Spirits have done it all in one night’.
Bells and clocks recur: the tolling of the bell before each Ghost creates suspense.
The Ghost of Christmas Present ages during his visit: time is short.
Stave 2: memory makes Scrooge feel again: ‘a thousand odours… each one connected with a thousand thoughts, and hopes, and joys, and cares long, long, forgotten!’
The Ghost’s light symbolises memory; Scrooge tries to put it out: the pain of remembering.
Memory explains the present: the lonely child becomes the lonely man.
Scrooge wishes he had given something to the carol singer and spoken kindly to Bob: small regrets lead to change.
Belle’s scenes: ‘Spirit! remove me from this place.’
Marley’s regret: ‘no space of regret can make amends for one life’s opportunity misused!’
Stave 4: the fear of a future no one regrets losing.
‘Are these the shadows of the things that Will be, or… things that May be, only?’: the future can change.
‘I will live in the Past, the Present, and the Future. The Spirits of all Three shall strive within me.’
Stave 5: ‘I don’t know what day of the month it is!’: time renewed; he has not missed Christmas.

callouts.p: Dickens uses time to show that the past shapes us, the present tests us, and the future can still be changed, so it is never too late to repent.

model: Vow to live in Past, Present and Future
exam.q: Explain the importance of memory and the past elsewhere in the novella. (20 marks)

mistakes.r: Scrooge discovers it all happened in one night.
mistakes.w: The Ghosts visit on three different nights.

quotes.a: Repetition shows how deeply memories were buried.

quotes.q: no space of regret can make amends for one life’s opportunity misused

quotes.a: Hope that the future can change.
Learning from past, present and future.
quotes.q: The Spirits of all Three shall strive within me

summary: Time, memory and regret structure the novella: the three Ghosts take Scrooge through past, present and future, memory awakens his regret, and his vow to ‘live in the Past, the Present, and the Future’ shows that learning from time is the key to redemption.
